claim.why_it_matters: Heading at the wrong level: it is a sibling of 4.3.1 Function, 4.3.3 Syntax Rules and 4.3.4 General Rules, all `###`, and is promoted to the level of its parent 4.3 (`##`).

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 536 (X-20) shows '4.3.2 General Format' as a numbered subsection of 4.3 THE DATA DESCRIPTION ENTRY IN THE INTER-PROGRAM COMMUNICATION MODULE. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md the parent is '## 4.3 ...' (line 20533), its siblings are '### 4.3.1 Function' (20535), '### 4.3.3 Syntax Rules' and '### 4.3.4 General Rules' (page 537), but this heading is '## 4.3.2 General Format' (20551), at the parent's level. The heading text is present and correct; only its level is wrong, so the defect is structural (document outline), not normative. The kind 'missing-heading' is imprecise: the heading is not missing, it is mis-leveled.
verdict.corrected_description: Heading level error, not a missing heading: '4.3.2 General Format' on page 536 is transcribed as '##' (the level of its parent 4.3) instead of '###' like its siblings 4.3.1, 4.3.3 and 4.3.4.
